sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target on SOL, traded forward through Kestrel on Binance's Spot Testnet, (a) behaves exactly as the backtest model says it should, and (b) keeps beating SOL held at the same average exposure on data that didn't exist when it was designed.
sections.rationale: On pursue since 2026-11-15 (Luke), the same rule as BTC: Sharpe 1.52 vs 1.24 over 2020-08 to 2025-10; fails luck (deflated 59%) and out of sample (2 of 6 windows); passed the holdout (+2.6% vs -13.8% for SOL at its exposure in a falling year). Only new data can settle luck. Its minimum track record (Bailey and Lopez de Prado, from its daily returns) is about 239 days for 90% confidence that its true Sharpe is above zero (393 for 95%); it runs 395 days, BTC's length, so all three coins are reviewed together. Each coin is its own account with its own 330 USDT, so one coin's result never hides another's. The testnet proves the plumbing; its prices come from Binance's test order book, so the strategy is judged on the model replay at real Binance prices, which makes the same decisions by construction. SOL pays a wider spread than BTC and ETH; testnet SOL liquidity may be thin, so plumbing failures there are reported, not treated as strategy results.
sections.rules: One account, tvt-sol: kestrel paper open tvt-sol --symbol SOLUSDT --strategy trend-vol-target --research <this note> --venue testnet --cash 330, then kestrel paper schedule tvt-sol (hourly at 10 past; idempotent). Default settings (20/60/120-day votes, 30-day volatility, 50% target), daily bars, the [risk] limits in kestrel.toml. Runs 395 days from its first decision. Reviewed every 3 months with kestrel paper track tvt-sol and the Trading page. Interim reviews report; only the 6-month check can end it, and only for failure (no stopping early on a good run).
sections.falsification: Plumbing, at every review: any decision that differs from the model is a bug, fixed before the test continues (not a strategy failure); missed days must stay under 5% of days handled. Early failure, at 182 days only: if the model replay is behind SOL held at its average exposure on both Sharpe and return, Claude recommends stopping and Luke decides; a good result at 182 days ends nothing. Strategy, at 395 days: the model replay must (1) have a probabilistic Sharpe of at least 90% (true Sharpe above zero), (2) beat SOL held at its average exposure over the whole period, by Sharpe if holding's Sharpe is positive and by return if it isn't (the holdout's rule), and (3) keep its worst drawdown no deeper than 50%. Failing any one means Claude recommends drop and Luke decides. A safety halt pauses the test for Luke to decide; it isn't resumed without a recorded reason.
sections.parameters: fast_days 20, mid_days 60, slow_days 120, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (the defaults; never changed during the test).
sections.costs: Modelled at kestrel.toml's costs (7.5 bps fees with the BNB discount, plus SOL's spread). Until the venue handles BNB fees, testnet fills pay 10 bps, so tracking will show fees slightly above the model. Paper trading is not a trial: nothing is chosen from it.
